# Stable Godot source-library discovery and on-demand reuse guidance

Status: Accepted, 2026-09-15.

The product already ships reusable visuals and gameplay, but the PI default prompt previously restricted reuse to an explicit player request. Authoring guidance prioritized only static scenery and described manual proposals even when the host allowed automatic installation. The modern read projection omitted the archive's verified dependencies. A late-discovered source-library tool also changed the request tool set unnecessarily.

Make targeted reuse the default starting point for Godot appearance and gameplay. Offer the existing registered source-library schema in the initial Godot PI profile, project exact dependencies on read, and align guidance with existing auto/manual installation routes. Expose the generated product asset index through the existing pinned, paginated guidance reference mechanism instead of injecting inventory or adding another world-source API.

No discovery result grants authority or proves gameplay. Existing archive hashes, source revisions, compatibility, instance identity, lease/permission checks and application evidence remain authoritative. A missing suitable asset does not block original authoring or justify a smaller player goal. The change does not introduce an exhaustive search protocol, a new budget or silent cross-world copying.
